descriptionChirho: To open a physical object such as a door, gate, window, sack, or container; the basic Qal active sense of physically opening something that was closed (Arabic فَتَحَ, Korean 열다, Swahili -fungua, Spanish abrir).
To open the mouth, lips, or eyes — a metaphorical extension of the basic 'open' sense used for body parts, often in speech acts or perception contexts (Arabic فَتَحَ, Korean 열다, Swahili -fungua).
State of being open, as a Qal passive participle describing doors, gates, eyes, or heavens that stand open (Arabic مَفْتُوح, Korean 열린, Swahili wazi, Spanish abierto/a).
To open or break forth, used intransitively of the earth opening, or of something bursting/breaking open (Korean 터지리라, 열렸으니; Swahili -funguka).
To draw or unsheathe a sword from its scabbard — a specialized Qal sense distinct from generic 'open' (Arabic سَلَّ, Spanish desenvainada/desenvainaron, Korean 빼다, Swahili -chomoa).
Nifal passive: to be opened, of doors, gates, heavens, eyes, or ears — the straightforward passive counterpart of the Qal 'open' sense (Arabic اِنْفَتَحَ, Korean 열리다, Swahili -funguliwa).

Piel intensive: to loose, untie, or unbind bonds, fetters, sackcloth, or a belt — cross-linguistically distinguished from 'open' by Arabic حَلَّ / فَكَّ, Korean 풀다, Spanish soltar/desatar, Swahili -fungua/-legeza.

Piel intensive: to set free, release, or liberate a person from captivity or bonds — a further development of the 'loose' sense applied to persons (Arabic أَطْلَقَ, Korean 놓아주다/풀어주다, Spanish liberar/soltar, Swahili -achia huru).
Nifal passive of the 'loose' sense: to be loosened, become unfastened — distinguished from 'be opened' by Arabic يَنفَكُّ and Korean 풀어지다.
Hitpael reflexive: to loose oneself, free oneself from bonds or chains — the reflexive counterpart of the Piel 'loose' sense (Arabic انْحَلِّي, Korean 풀라).
